subject: Box plot in example file "Weather" not displaying correctly

messages.author: 64e8a55751780494
messages.subject: Box plot in example file "Weather" not displaying correctly
parts:
Hello All,

Is anyone else having issues with the Rattle box plot display using
the wetaher dataset?

When i first executed the file as per Peters instructions graphs 1, 2
and 3 were displaying incorrectly, then i unselected use Cairo
Graphics and all but graph 1 was correct.

graph 1 refers to the Box plot of the Rainfall variable using
Distributions type.

The appearance suggest the data is exceeding some boundary? see the R-
code below.

#============================================================
# Rattle timestamp: 2010-12-01 16:23:30 i386-pc-mingw32

# Box Plot

# Subset the data for a boxplot of the variable Rainfall with the
appropriate groups.

ds <- rbind(data.frame(dat=crs$dataset[crs$sample,][,"Rainfall"],
grp="All"),
data.frame(dat=crs$dataset[crs$sample,][crs$dataset[crs
$sample,]$RainTomorrow=="No","Rainfall"], grp="No"),
data.frame(dat=crs$dataset[crs$sample,][crs$dataset[crs
$sample,]$RainTomorrow=="Yes","Rainfall"], grp="Yes"))

# Plot the data, grouped appropriately.

bp <- boxplot(formula=dat ~ grp, data=ds, col=rainbow_hcl(3),
xlab="RainTomorrow", ylab="Rainfall", notch=TRUE)

# The 'doBy' package provides the 'summaryBy' function.

require(doBy, quietly=TRUE)

# Calculate the group means.

points(1:3, summaryBy(dat ~ grp, data=ds, FUN=mean, na.rm=TRUE)
$dat.mean, pch=8)

# Add a title to the plot.

title(main="Distribution of Rainfall (sample)
by RainTomorrow", sub=paste("Rattle", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%b-%d %H:
%M:%S"), Sys.info()["user"]))

messages.subject: Re: Box plot in example file "Weather" not displaying correctly
parts:
Thanks for the error report.

It looks like a problem with Cairo and boxplot (i.e., perhaps not specifically a Rattle problem - alhotugh perhaps it is related to how Rattle generates the data to be plotted).

Could you send the output of 

> rattle.info()

and a screen shot of the plot(s).

It all looks okay for me on Linux, but I see some oddities on Windows.

Regards,
Graham
